content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: no-cost rebalance. Delay the 12:30-13:00 breaks by 30 minutes and swap 2 cross-skilled agents between queues later. This is predicted to give 95.8% service level for 12:30-14:30, against an 80% target.","why":"Since 12:00, agents on the phones have fallen below plan in both queues. Payments had 24 and then 23 against 31 and 29 planned. General had 24 and then 21 against 27 planned. Service level dropped to 19.6% and 47.4% in payments and 24.7% and 11.7% in general. The attendance feed shows no absences and no incident explains the gap, so the cause is unknown. Check for off-plan breaks or meetings, or a phone or login problem. General volume is also 26.6% over forecast. P1 costs nothing and breaks no policy. It is predicted to reach 96.4% in payments and 95.1% in general over the window, with 1.2% abandons and 96.6% for the rest of the day.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) is also predicted to meet target at 92.8%, but P1 adds margin at no cost. That margin matters while the cause of the drop is unknown.","P3 (chat deflection) is slightly stronger at 96.5% with 0.8% abandons, but costs INR 336 and pushes some customers to chat.","P2 (callbacks) costs nothing but predicts only 92.8%, with higher abandons at 1.6% and general at 92.0%.","P4 (overtime) costs INR 360 for 92.8%, no better than doing nothing in the window.","P1's agent moves take cover from one queue to help the other. General is still predicted at 95.1%, so the risk to it looks low."],"watch":"Confirm agents actually come back on the phones and find why staffing dropped. These predictions assume staffing recovers. If agent counts stay below plan, or general volume keeps running about 27% over forecast and service level slips toward 80%, reconsider P3."}
